Lower EMI or Shorter Tenure?

When you part-prepay, most lenders let you either keep the EMI and finish sooner, or keep the end date and lower the EMI. Keeping the EMI usually saves more interest. Lowering it gives you more breathing room each month.

Example: ₹40,00,000 at 8.50% with 20 years left, and a ₹5,00,000 part-payment today. Keeping the EMI at ₹34,713 finishes the loan 62 months early and saves ₹16,71,631 in interest. Lowering the EMI to ₹30,374 saves ₹5,41,388.

How to Use This Calculator

  1. Enter your outstanding balance, rate and remaining tenure from your latest statement
  2. Add a lump sum, a monthly extra payment or both
  3. Add any prepayment fee, which is usually zero on an individual's floating-rate loan
  4. Compare the net saving and new EMI under each option

The calculation assumes your rate stays the same. On a floating loan it will move, so treat the saving as an estimate.

Frequently Asked Questions

Should I reduce my EMI or my tenure after a prepayment?
Reducing tenure usually saves more interest, because you keep repaying at the higher amount. Reducing the EMI leaves more cash free each month, which can matter more if your income is tight or uncertain. The calculator above shows the difference for your loan.
Are there charges for prepaying a home loan in India?
Lenders cannot charge individuals pre-payment fees on floating-rate loans taken for non-business purposes. Fixed-rate loans can carry charges, and a hybrid loan's treatment depends on whether it is on a floating rate when you pre-pay. Check your loan agreement.
When should I prepay my home loan?
Earlier generally saves more, because interest is charged on a larger balance in the early years. Before prepaying, keep an emergency fund and consider paying off costlier debts such as credit cards first.
Is it better to prepay or invest?
Prepaying earns a certain return equal to your loan rate, while investing may earn more but with risk. Tax matters too, since any deduction on home loan interest lowers its real cost under the old regime. Many borrowers do some of both.
Does prepaying affect my tax deduction?
It can. Paying less interest may reduce any deduction you claim on home loan interest under the old regime, and that deduction is generally unavailable for a self-occupied home under the new regime. This calculator does not include tax.
